title: Subdomain takeover: `developer-ai-radar.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz` CNAMEs to an unregistered GitHub Pages account
vulnerability_information:
`developer-ai-radar.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz` is a DNS record under `expedia.biz` that still CNAMEs to `eg-internal.github.io`. No GitHub account named
`eg-internal` exists: `github.com/eg-internal`, `api.github.com/users/eg-internal` and `eg-internal.github.io` all answer `404`.
The namespace is free to register, so whoever registers `eg-internal` first inherits every hostname that
points at it — including TLS certificates GitHub issues automatically once the domain is claimed.

The same unclaimed namespace carries 2 more hostnames, every one of them still answering:

```
  developer-ai-radar.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz
  devex-mcp-registry.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz
  egds-components-android.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz
```

This is a classic dangling-CNAME takeover: the DNS record outlived the repository that owned it.

## Evidence

Record verified live at filing time:

```
$ dig +short developer-ai-radar.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz CNAME
eg-internal.github.io

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://developer-ai-radar.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz/
302            # -> https://github.com/pages/auth

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://github.com/eg-internal
404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://api.github.com/users/eg-internal
404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://eg-internal.github.io/
404
```

The three `404`s are the finding. The `302` to `/pages/auth` alone would not be evidence: GitHub
returns the same redirect for a *private* Pages site, so it only becomes a takeover when the account
and the native site are both absent.

I did not register `eg-internal` or publish anything — claiming the name would have been an intrusive step
against production and creating the account needs a human at a captcha. Ping me and I will complete
the claim inside whatever window suits you.

## Remediation

Remove the CNAME for every hostname listed above, or recreate the `eg-internal` GitHub account and a Pages
repository so the names resolve to content you control. Audit the zone for other records pointing at
`*.github.io` — this set alone had 3.

## Live re-verification (2026-11-07T16:18Z)

All three hostnames were re-checked immediately before filing:

```
$ dig +short developer-ai-radar.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz CNAME
eg-internal.github.io.
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}' https://developer-ai-radar.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz/
302 -> https://github.com/pages/auth?nonce=...&page_id=59532645&path=Lw

$ dig +short egds-components-android.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz CNAME
eg-internal.github.io.
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}' https://egds-components-android.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz/
302 -> https://github.com/pages/auth?nonce=...&page_id=62810651&path=Lw

$ dig +short devex-mcp-registry.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz CNAME
eg-internal.github.io.
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://devex-mcp-registry.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz/
404

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://api.github.com/users/eg-internal
404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://eg-internal.github.io/
404
```

The TLS certificate served for `devex-mcp-registry.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz` is GitHub's
wildcard `CN=*.github.io` (Let's Encrypt, 2026-09-30 → 2026-12-29), not a per-domain certificate:
GitHub's edge is still answering for these names, but no Pages site is provisioned behind them.

The two distinct `page_id` values (59532645, 62810651) are GitHub's own records for those custom
domains — GitHub remembers the names and will hand them to whichever account claims
`eg-internal.github.io` first.

I have **not** registered the `eg-internal` account, published a page, or changed any DNS record.
impact:
An attacker who registers the free `eg-internal` account and enables Pages can publish arbitrary content
on `https://developer-ai-radar.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz/`, under the organisation's own domain and a valid certificate. That is enough to
host phishing that survives a glance at the URL bar, to impersonate whatever the hostnames claim to be
(documentation, developer tooling, internal services — the names above are the ones this namespace
carries), and to intercept users who follow old links or bookmarks. No user interaction beyond visiting
the hostname is required.
